system_note: Reviewed revenue line: billed Rev Code 0192 (rehabilitation therapy), 12 units, DOS range 02/03/2026-02/23/2026. Facility documentation includes repeated daily Skilled Nursing Progress Notes within the claim range that explicitly record the per-diem as Level 1 (Rev 0191) on multiple days (see nursing notes cited below). The facility's own daily notes are a direct statement of the per-diem level the clinician assigned for those dates and take precedence over an auditor's inference from therapy minutes when they exist. Although PT/OT evaluation and the interdisciplinary plan document an ordered program of therapy (frequency 5x/week) and justify skilled rehabilitation services in principle, the facility's daily nursing notes within the billed range state Level 1 per diem (Rev 0191) on several dates, indicating the clinical record does not support the billed 0192 level for those documented days and therefore those 12 billed 0192 units must be downcoded to 0191. Key supporting/contradicting passages relied on (see evidence_cited for full quotes and document/page mapping): - Skilled Nursing Progress Notes: multiple entries within the DOS range explicitly state Level 1 per diem (Rev 0191) (ev1, ev2, ev3, ev4). These are direct daily level statements coming from the facility's clinical notes and contradict the submitted 0192 billing for those days. - PT/OT evaluation and interdisciplinary plan of care document an active therapy program with frequency 5x/week (ev5, ev6) and thus support that therapy was ordered and delivered on many days, but they do not override the facility's daily per-diem statements when those exist. - Reference guidance defines revenue codes 0191/0192 and the concept of a Non-covered day (ev7) and supports per-day adjustment (downcoding) rather than denying the entire stay when documentation for a specific billed per-diem level is not present. Determination and correction applied: Finding. The 12 units billed at 0192 are not supported at the 0192 (rehabilitation therapy) per-diem level in the record for the days the facility documented Level 1; those 12 units will be recoded to 0191 (skilled nursing) for the billed DOS range 02/03/2026-02/23/2026. Rationale: facility daily notes explicitly state Level 1 per diem on dates within the billed range (contradicting the billed 0192) (ev1-ev4); policy permits per-day adjustments when documentation fails to support the billed per-diem (ev7). Audit reviewer: Senior Clinical Claims Auditor. See evidence_cited entries for the exact verbatim source passages (document/section/page) relied upon. Claim MR_SNF_06 - Revenue line 2 billed as 0191 (skilled nursing) for 8 days 2026-02-03 to 2026-02-23. The facility's therapy documentation (PT and OT sessions) shows regular involvement of licensed therapy staff on multiple dates within the billed range (e.g. 2026-02-03, 02-04, 02-05, 02-06, 02-09, 02-10, 02-11, 02-12, 02-13, 02-16, 02-17, 02-18, 02-19, 02-20, 02-23) with per-session minutes recorded (PT 60 min + OT 45 min = 105 min on treatment dates). get_per_diem_level_notes returned no explicit per-diem-level exceptions for these dates (null level_determination_statement), which per the tool's note commonly means the billed level's own documentation thresholds were met rather than that the day is unsupported. The payer-agnostic SNF reference defines the governing concepts: Skilled need is a service requiring licensed nursing or therapy staff and that cannot be safely or effectively provided by non-skilled caregivers (policy: Skilled need), and revenue code 0191 maps to the skilled nursing level (policy: Revenue codes 0191-0194). Given the presence of licensed therapy services on the dates within the billed range and the reference definition of skilled need, the clinical record supports billing at the 0191 skilled nursing per-diem level for the full date range billed. Note: there is no payer-specific SNF per-diem guideline available in the dataset for Aetna Medicare Advantage, so this determination used the payer-agnostic Level of Care reference guide as the governing policy.
rationale_letter: Re: MR_SNF_06 - Per-Diem Line Review (Rev Code 0192, billed 12 days, 02/03/2026-02/23/2026) Dear Provider, We completed an audit of the above-referenced SNF per-diem revenue line. The claim billed 12 days of rehabilitation therapy (Rev Code 0192) for the period 02/03/2026-02/23/2026. Based on a review of the medical record, we have determined the documentation does not support the billed 0192 per-diem level for those 12 days. Basis for Finding: - The facility's own Skilled Nursing Progress Notes within the billed DOS range explicitly document the per-diem level as Level 1 (Rev 0191) on multiple days (see cited nursing progress notes). These are direct, day-specific level determinations recorded by facility clinicians and therefore control the per-day level-of-care assignment. - Although the PT and OT evaluations and the interdisciplinary plan of care document an ordered therapy program (frequency 5x/week) and show therapy was provided on many days, the explicit per-diem entries in the daily nursing notes contradict billing the days at Rev Code 0192. - Under the SNF level-of-care guidance, when documentation for a specific billed per-diem level is not present for an individual day, that day must be adjusted (per-day downcoding), not the entire stay. Correction Applied: - The 12 days billed at Rev Code 0192 are not supported as 0192 in the record for the documented dates and will be recoded to Rev Code 0191 (skilled nursing) for the DOS range 02/03/2026-02/23/2026. This is a per-day downcode (12 units recoded to 0191). If you believe there is additional documentation that substantiates Rev Code 0192 for those specific billed days (for example, explicit daily level determinations or separate daily therapy-level statements contradicting the nursing notes), please submit those records with date- and time-stamped pages and indicate the exact dates that should remain at Rev Code 0192. We will reconsider the determination upon receipt of such documentation. Sincerely, Senior Clinical Claims Auditor
